overview: Two categories of antibiotic reach, reflecting a fundamental antimicrobial stewardship trade-off between precision and coverage.
genZNote: Narrow-spectrum: a scalpel. Broad-spectrum: a sledgehammer.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: Antibiotics effective against a limited range of bacteria, often just Gram-positive or Gram-negative organisms.
aspects.valueB: Antibiotics effective against a wide range of both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria.

aspects.label: Target Range
aspects.valueA: Targeted, e.g. penicillin G against many Gram-positive cocci.
aspects.valueB: Wide, e.g. tetracyclines or carbapenems covering many Gram-positive, Gram-negative, and sometimes atypical organisms.

aspects.label: Clinical Use Case
aspects.valueA: Preferred once the causative organism and susceptibility are known (targeted, de-escalated therapy).
aspects.valueB: Preferred for empiric therapy when the causative organism is unknown or infection is severe/polymicrobial.

aspects.label: Impact on Normal Microbiota
aspects.valueB: Greater disruption to normal microbiota, increasing risk of superinfection (e.g. Clostridioides difficile).

aspects.label: Resistance Considerations
aspects.valueA: Lower selective pressure for broad resistance development.
aspects.valueB: Higher selective pressure, contributing more to antimicrobial resistance if overused.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Effective against a limited group of organisms.
aspects.valueB: Effective against a wide variety of organisms.
